_comment: Copy for the 'How this works' page (#/how). English is design's draft and UNREVIEWED by the user; fi and sv are deliberately empty until the user writes them, and the page refuses to render in a language whose lede is blank. Layout lives in index.html because the structure is fixed and approved; only the words live here, so revising them is cheap. Inline markup: **bold**, *italic*, [text](url) — nothing else, and everything is escaped before it is applied.
_liveComment: Which languages this page is PUBLISHED in. Separate from whether a translation exists, because those are different facts: a draft translation can sit in this file without going live. A language appears on the site only if it is listed here AND its text is written. Absent or empty means English only. Adding a code here is the act of publishing, and it is the user's to make after reading that language.

lede.en: Before you send us a list, here is exactly what we hold, what you control, and what belongs here.

zonesLeft.en: What is sold, hidden, or in negotiation

zonesNote.en: We hold no buyer details at all. Messages go through your own form straight to your Tally inbox — **we never see them.** Nothing about a buyer is ever stored on this site, so there is nothing here to leak, sell, or ask us to delete.

splitTitle.en: What you change, and what you ask for

splitNowSub.en: no login, works on a phone

splitNow.en: Hide a wishlist entry you have found

splitAskSub.en: a form on the same page

splitAsk.en: Fixing specs, HP, or power draw

splitNote.en: **You control the facts only you know** — what sold, what it costs, whether you will haggle. **We handle the parts that need work** — photographing it, checking the specs, drawing the panel to scale, writing it in three languages.

whyTitle.en: Why it is built this way

why.en: This is a hobby project. A couple of people, evenings.

There are two ways to build something like this. One assumes nobody can be trusted: accounts, passwords, moderation, spam defences, and a plan for the day someone abuses it. That is a swamp of a project that never stops asking for attention.
The other assumes **you** can be trusted, because we know who you are. It is a fraction of the work and it stays small.
We are doing the second one — and honestly, the first one would not exist. Not because it is a worse idea, but because nobody here wants to spend their evenings running it.

**That is also why we ask for more than eight modules, and why someone vouches for you if we do not know you.** That trust is doing the job a login screen would otherwise be doing. It is not gatekeeping for its own sake — it is the thing holding the whole arrangement up.
What you get out of it: no account to make, no password to forget, one link that works on a phone. What you give up: you cannot add or rewrite content yourself, and new things wait for us.

rulesYes.en: Odd sound things: strange headphones, contact mics, unusual pedals

rulesTest.en: The test is whether someone in the Finnish eurorack group would stop scrolling at it. Weird headphones, yes. Baby clothes, no. A generic alarm clock, no — a strange one someone built, probably yes.

rulesCall.en: Suggest whatever you like. In the end we decide, because we built this and would rather not spend the evenings arguing about it.

step1.en: **A list of your modules** — including ones you are not selling yet. Everything arrives hidden, so nothing goes public until you say so.
**Prices** for the ones you would sell.
**A wishlist** — what you are looking for.

**A way for buyers to reach you.** A Tally form of your own — enquiries land in your Tally inbox, and by email too if you switch notifications on. Or honestly any page where someone can contact you — your own site's contact form is fine.

step1Tail.en: **Your email address**, so we can send you your link. This one is for us, not for buyers.

formBoxLead.en: **Include a question asking which module they mean.** It is the one thing tying an enquiry to an item. Without it, messages arrive reading *“is this still available?”* with no way to tell what *this* is. Our side helps: the contact link on each module page shows the buyer that module's name, so it is sitting in front of them to copy.

formBoxFour.en: **Which module are you asking about?** — the one that matters

formBoxNoForm.en: **No form yet?** [tally.so](https://tally.so) is free and takes about five minutes. Make an account, add those four questions, publish, and send us the link. Switch on *email notifications* while you are there, or you will only see enquiries when you next open it.

_sendHrefComment: Points at the general contact form for now. The user intends a dedicated joining form later — swap this value and nothing else changes; the sentence works either way.

sendVia.en: Send it all through [the contact form on eurorack.fi]({href}).

step2.en: We add every module's details — photos, specs, HP, power, panel drawing, and the description in three languages.
We send you your own link.

step3.en: Unhide whatever you actually want to sell.
From then on it is yours — sold, negotiation, prices, wishlist.

contactsNote.en: **Two different contacts, and they are not the same thing.** The contact form is public and is how buyers reach you — we never see those messages. Your email address is private and is only used to send you your link.

batchNote.en: Adding something new later — an item or a wishlist entry — means asking us, and we deal with those in batches every few weeks rather than daily. Everything you can change yourself is instant. It is only new content that waits.

ai.en: This entire project has been made with AI. That means there will be inevitable mistakes and inaccuracies — but we hope the human and personal component of this (the fact that we are a community and not strangers on the internet) will smooth over those *“the site has the wrong colour panel shown”* moments.
